blueprint.system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
blueprint.competency_task: Selects the most likely neurologic diagnosis from a localizing examination.

difficulty.rationale: Requires integration of discriminating clinical clues with a mechanism or diagnosis rather than isolated fact recall.

option_audit.correct: The complete ocular motor and pupillary triad with a pineal-region lesion is diagnostic of Parinaud syndrome.
option_audit.INO: Would cause impaired adduction with abducting nystagmus rather than vertical-gaze and pretectal pupillary findings.
option_audit.one_and_a_half: Produces a pontine horizontal-gaze pattern, not dorsal-midbrain upgaze failure.
option_audit.Weber: Produces ipsilateral CN III palsy with contralateral hemiparesis from ventral midbrain injury.
option_audit.Adie: Can mimic the pupillary component only; it cannot account for the central vertical-gaze and convergence-retraction signs.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A pineal-region mass with obstructive-hydrocephalus symptoms plus conjugate upgaze palsy, convergence-retraction nystagmus and light-near dissociation localizes to the dorsal rostral midbrain/pretectum and defines Parinaud syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Adie tonic pupil can show light-near dissociation, but it cannot explain conjugate upgaze palsy, convergence-retraction nystagmus or the dorsal midbrain mass.
adversarial_second_pass.other_distractors: INO and one-and-a-half syndrome are MLF/pontine horizontal eye-movement syndromes; Weber syndrome is a ventral midbrain oculomotor-plus-contralateral-motor syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: The pineal mass is an appropriate localization clue but the diagnosis still requires integrating three eye-movement/pupillary findings.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No unsupported percentage, tumor histology assumption or pressure threshold is stated.
